skill.name: repurpose-into-a-post
skill.description: Turn an article, newsletter, transcript, video or long document into a Twitter or LinkedIn post that stands on its own. Use when someone wants to repurpose existing content, share a link, promote a piece they published, or turn a recording or long draft into something postable. Do not use it to write from scratch, and do not produce a summary with a link attached.
skill.summary: Turn existing long-form content into standalone Twitter or LinkedIn posts, preserving specific evidence and adapting the writing to each platform.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Turn Long-Form Content Into Standalone Social Posts
content.value_statement: Long articles and transcripts often become social posts that offer little value without a click. This skill selects one claim and supporting detail to create a standalone Twitter or LinkedIn post.
actual_capabilities: Identify two or three distinct claims from supplied content and ask the user to select one.
Preserve a specific number, result, mistake, or quotation that supports the selected claim.
Draft claim-first Twitter posts or LinkedIn posts with context, a claim, and reader implications.
Remove spoken filler and false starts when adapting transcripts into written posts.
Present link placement choices and offer unused claims as candidates for later posts.
Use connected VoiceMOAT tools for platform voice profiles, voice matching, draft improvement, and scheduling with preview and confirmation.
limitations: Requires existing source content; it is not intended for writing posts from scratch.
Provides no video transcription or URL retrieval implementation; source access depends on the host environment.
VoiceMOAT features require a connected service and a Pro or Enterprise plan.
Does not guarantee engagement, validate source claims independently, or establish precise platform link penalties.

use_cases.title: Adapt a published newsletter
use_cases.description: Select a newsletter claim and supporting detail, then draft a standalone LinkedIn post with a chosen link placement.

use_cases.title: Reuse interview material
use_cases.description: Turn a supplied interview transcript into a focused Twitter post while removing spoken filler and preserving the relevant quotation.

use_cases.title: Plan posts from a detailed article
use_cases.description: Separate an article into distinct claims, draft the selected post, and offer remaining claims for future posts.

prompt_templates.title: Repurpose an article
prompt_templates.prompt: Repurpose this article into a LinkedIn post: [article text]. Show two or three candidate claims and let me choose before drafting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: selecting one idea from existing content.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a transcript
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this transcript into a Twitter post: [transcript]. Ask me to select a claim, preserve one concrete detail, and remove spoken filler.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: converting speech into concise written content.

prompt_templates.title: Create platform-specific drafts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this source: [source text]. After I select a claim, draft Twitter and LinkedIn versions. Keep its supporting evidence and ask about link placement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: adapting the same claim to two platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare voice-matched follow-up posts
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract distinct claims from [newsletter]. Let me select the first. Use connected VoiceMOAT tools to match my LinkedIn voice. Preview and confirm each scheduled post.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: optional voice matching and confirmed scheduling with VoiceMOAT.

output_examples.input: Twitter draft request after claim selection. Source: a team reduced onboarding from six steps to three, and completion rose from 48% to 67%. No link.
output_examples.output: Fewer onboarding steps can matter more than more guidance. We reduced ours from six to three, and completion rose from 48% to 67%.

output_examples.input: LinkedIn draft request after claim selection. Transcript: support tickets fell from 120 to 80 weekly after a team rewrote one confusing setup instruction.
output_examples.output: Our team kept answering the same setup question. We rewrote one confusing instruction, and weekly support tickets fell from 120 to 80. Before expanding support, check whether your instructions create avoidable questions.

best_practices: Provide accessible source text and verify the selected numbers, results, and quotations before publishing.
Choose one claim, the target platform, and a link placement before finalizing the draft.
Review voice-matched drafts and confirm each scheduled post individually when using VoiceMOAT.
anti_patterns: Compress every source idea into one post or repeat the same claim across several posts.
Replace the post with a short summary that requires readers to click for its main value.
Invent supporting evidence or cite precise link penalty percentages without reliable evidence.

faq.question: What source material can I repurpose?
faq.answer: The workflow covers articles, newsletters, transcripts, recordings, and long documents. Provide readable source content when your environment cannot access or transcribe the original.

faq.question: Can this skill write posts from scratch?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to repurpose existing material and asks you to select a claim before drafting.

faq.question: Which platforms does it support?
faq.answer: It gives separate writing guidance for Twitter and LinkedIn. Twitter starts with the claim; LinkedIn adds context and reader implications.

faq.question: Will every post include a link?
faq.answer: No. It asks you to choose no link, a link in a reply or comment, or a link in the post.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: No. Basic repurposing does not require VoiceMOAT. Its optional voice and scheduling tools require a connection and a Pro or Enterprise plan.

faq.question: Does the skill publish posts automatically?
faq.answer: The file includes no publishing implementation. Optional VoiceMOAT scheduling is described as requiring a preview and confirmation for each post.
